title: Anthropic clamps down on Claude’s AI video game clones
summary: Anthropic updates Claude Code system prompt to prevent video game cloning
detailed: Anthropic has updated Claude Code's system prompt on Opus 5.5 to prevent the AI from re-creating specific existing video games.
The change is intended to stop the tool from being used to infringe on intellectual property, which violates Anthropic's usage policy.
Users are still permitted to build original games, genre games, and games derived from their own designs and assets.
sentences: Anthropic is steering Claude away from re-creating specific titles, but users can still use it to make their own games.

Anthropic has updated Claude Code’s system prompt to prevent the AI tool from being used to re-create existing video games, as reported by Tom’s Hardware .

Retro gaming is currently being overrun with AI-made decompilations, recompilations, and ports , but while Anthropic will still let people use Claude Code to make games, it doesn’t want people to use it for direct clones.

Last week, a user on X posted a screenshot allegedly showing two new sentences added to Claude Code’s system prompt: “Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets.
Original games, genre games, and games built from your own designs and assets are meant to keep working.
We’ll continue to iterate to ensure we’re striking the right balance.
In the meantime, if Claude turns down something that’s yours, send it my way.
We’ve asked Anthropic if it has or will be updating other Claude system prompts as well.
